LESSON: READING 10.4.1 PLAY: PROJECT

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does an acted play differ from a written one?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 10.4.1 PLAY: PROJECT
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 10.4.1 PLAY: PROJECT
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere

What this means
In this part you learn to identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does an acted play differ from a written one?
2. What makes a performance successful?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 10.4.1 Play: Project means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify simple props and costumes that create mood and atmosphere.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
